diverge.why: V8 exposes no per-iteration allocation count. Node offers heap totals through process.memoryUsage and v8.getHeapStatistics, and neither counts allocations, so there is no number to hold to a ceiling.
diverge.remedy: A counter in V8's API, or a profiler sampling allocations, which is too slow to run per iteration.

diverge.why: V8 exposes no allocation count, for the reason the bench-max-allocs entry gives, so there is no count per call to hold to a ceiling.
diverge.remedy: The counter in V8's API that bench-max-allocs needs.

diverge.why: Bytes allocated per iteration can only be read as a heap-usage delta, which moves with whether the collector ran. Measuring one unchanged body six times gave 43, -3, 43, -10, -10 and -8 bytes per iteration, so a ceiling set from one run fails the next for no reason.
diverge.remedy: A per-iteration allocation total that does not depend on collector timing.

limits.what: Accepts no relaxations, where the other implementations let a caller equate NaNs or an absent container with an empty one for this call.
limits.why: An oversight rather than a decision: equal, notEqual, contains and notContains all take them here and isPure does not. It is recorded rather than fixed quietly so the gap is visible until it closes.

limits.what: Reports no call site. The assertion awaits the subject, and by the time it reports, the caller's frame has left the stack.
limits.why: V8 gives an async function no synchronous caller frame once it has awaited. The standard states a location as optional for this reason, and every assertion that does not await carries one.

limits.what: Carries no lock. The runtime has one thread, so two assertions cannot report at the same instant.
limits.why: The standard asks that a seat be usable from more than one thread. A runtime with one thread meets that without doing anything, and says so here rather than leaving a reader to work out which it is.

limits.what: Runs one case at a time, whatever the number of workers. The run reports what a run on one worker reports, as it does in every language.
limits.why: A body runs on the runtime's one thread. An asynchronous body would interleave with another case at each await instead of running beside it, and a body that is not safe to interleave with itself would then fail in a way that a run on one worker never shows.

surface.why: The seat states report and clock itself, with a default, so a seat that supplies neither gets the platform clock and a rendered sentence. Only a language whose interfaces carry no defaults needs a second interface to say the same thing.

The harness owns the loop here, so setup goes in a second closure, handed to measuring, that the harness runs outside the measurement. Marking the setup in place would need the body to reach the contract it was handed to.

equal and notEqual hold want to the type of got through NoInfer, so the static form already rejects a mismatched pair at compile time. A chain would be a second way to write what is checked either way.
